mainTopic: Burial on יום טוב, attachments on שבת, the limits of הערמה, and straining wine on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story: רבי יוחנן ruled that non-Jews should bury someone who died on a יום טוב next to שבת. רבא then gives the rule. On the first day of יום טוב non-Jews bury, while on the second day Jews may bury, even on the second day of ראש השנה. רב מנשיא's earlier ban applied only to people who were not learned in Torah. Next, רב חמא בר גוריא allows wearing a canopy with its straps outside on שבת, because the straps are unimportant and become part of it, unlike ציצית. רבה בר רב הונא allows a trick (הערמה) of hanging a strainer for pomegranates on יום טוב, and רב אשי requires that pomegranates actually be hung in it, because otherwise the act looks forbidden. רב אשי also defends a young scholar's pretexts, since they involved only rabbinic rules and a scholar will not come to break them outright. A new משנה then permits straining wine that is already drinkable. The גמרא limits this with several conditions: only clear liquids, no hollow in the cloth, the basket kept low, and nothing that looks like a strainer. The amud ends by starting יעקב קרחה's explanation of the egg in a mustard strainer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules that non-Jews should handle the burial
steps.stepSummary: The story ends. The teller did not know whether the יום טוב was before or after שבת, and רבי יוחנן ruled that non-Jews should take care of the dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I do not know whether it was before it or after it. They came before רבי יוחנן, and he told them: Let non-Jews take care of him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story about someone who died on a יום טוב that was next to שבת. רבי יוחנן's ruling was that non-Jews should handle the burial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teller remembers the ruling but not whether the יום טוב came before or after שבת. The key point does not depend on that detail. On this day, Jews themselves should not do the burial work, and עממין (non-Jews) should do it instead.

keyTerms.meaning: let them take care of him (his burial)

phrases.english: And I do not know whether before it
phrases.notes: The יום טוב was next to שבת. The teller forgot on which side.

phrases.english: or after it
And they came before Rabbi Yochanan
and he said to them: Let non-Jews attend to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a story that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When someone dies on such a יום טוב, non-Jews should handle the burial.

steps.title: רבא's rule: first day versus second day of יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that on the first day of יום טוב non-Jews bury the dead, but on the second day Jews may do it. This holds even on the second day of ראש השנה, unlike the law of an egg.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: If someone died on the first day of יום טוב, non-Jews should take care of him. On the second day of יום טוב, Jews may take care of him, even on the second day of ראש השנה. That is not the case with an egg.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a general rule for burial on יום טוב. He splits the first day from the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first day is Torah-level, so Jews may not do the burial work, and non-Jews do it. The second day (יום טוב שני) is only rabbinic, so out of respect for the dead the חכמים let Jews bury, even on the second day of ראש השנה. This is unusual because for a ביצה (an egg laid on the first day) the two days of ראש השנה are treated as one long day, so the egg stays forbidden on the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: the first day of the festival (Torah-level)
the second festival day kept outside ארץ ישראל (rabbinic)
the New Year festival, whose two days have a special status

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the second day of ראש השנה is just like any other second day. For an egg, its two days count as one long day, which makes it stricter. Still, for burial רבא is lenient even there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the practical הלכה on burying the dead on the second day of יום טוב.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
A dead person on the first day of a festival
non-Jews should attend to him
on the second day of a festival
Jews may attend to him

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בְּיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה.
phrases.english: and even on the second day of Rosh HaShanah
which is not so regarding an egg.
phrases.notes: An egg laid on the first day of ראש השנה stays forbidden on the second day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the burial story into a general rule that separates the first day from the second day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First day of יום טוב: non-Jews bury. Second day, even of ראש השנה: Jews may bury.

steps.title: Why רב מנשיא forbade the people of בשכר
steps.stepSummary: This explains why רב מנשיא, earlier on the daf, did not let the people of בשכר bury on יום טוב. They were not learned in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. If Jews may bury on the second day, why did רב מנשיא stop the people of בשכר? The answer is that they were not learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law itself allows Jews to bury on the second day. But people who are not בני תורה might take יום טוב lightly and come to treat it like a weekday. So רב מנשיא's ban was a special safeguard for that community, not a change in the basic law.
steps.whatToRemember: The leniency for the second day of יום טוב can be held back from communities who might come to belittle יום טוב.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not explain the egg rule just before it. It answers an implied question about רב מנשיא and the people of בשכר from earlier on the daf.

phrases.english: Because they are not people of Torah.
phrases.notes: This refers to the people of בשכר, whom רב מנשיא forbade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between רבא's lenient rule and רב מנשיא's earlier ban.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the earlier ban to a specific community
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב מנשיא's ban seems to say Jews may never bury on the second day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban was a safeguard for people who were not learned. The basic law stays lenient.

steps.title: Wearing a canopy with its straps on Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא rules that a person may wrap himself in a canopy, together with its straps, and go out into the public domain on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין בר רב הונא said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא: A person may wrap himself in a canopy and its straps and go out to the public domain on שבת, and he need not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. A canopy wrapped around the body counts as clothing, and its attached straps do not count as a separate load being carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wearing clothing is not considered carrying on שבת. The question is whether the כסכסים (straps) are a separate item. This ruling says they are not, so there is no worry about הוצאה (carrying out).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin bar Rav Huna said
that Rav Chama bar Gurya said:
A person may wrap himself in a canopy and its straps
and go out to the public domain on Shabbat
and he need not be concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to burial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Canopy straps become part of the wrapped canopy. Wearing it out on שבת is not carrying.

steps.title: Challenge from a garment without proper ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this differs from רב הונא's ruling. Going out on שבת in a טלית without proper ציצית makes one liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from רב הונא? רב הונא said in the name of רב: One who goes out on שבת in a טלית that does not have proper ציצית is liable to bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חמא בר גוריא. In another case, strings attached to a garment are treated as a separate load, so why not the canopy straps?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Invalid ציצית strings are attached to the garment, yet רב says wearing it counts as carrying them, so one is liable. That suggests attachments do not automatically become part of the garment. If so, canopy straps should also count as a load.

keyTerms.meaning: liable to bring a sin-offering (for an accidental Torah violation)

phrases.english: What is different from Rav Huna's ruling?
For Rav Huna said in the name of Rav:
One who goes out in a garment
that does not have proper ritual fringes, on Shabbat
is liable to a sin-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 4 with a ruling that seems to contradict it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חמא בר גוריא's ruling that canopy straps are not a load
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Invalid ציצית attached to a garment do count as a load. So attached straps should count as a load too.

steps.title: ציצית are significant, canopy straps are not
steps.stepSummary: ציצית are important compared to the garment, so they are not cancelled out and count as a load. Canopy straps are not important, so they are cancelled out into the canopy.
steps.simpleTranslation: ציצית compared to a טלית are significant and are not nullified. These straps are not significant and are nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It draws a line between attachments that are important and those that are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An attachment becomes part of the garment (בטל) only if it is unimportant. ציצית are חשיבי, significant items in their own right. Even when they are invalid they keep a separate identity, so carrying them out is a violation. Canopy straps have no such importance and simply become part of the canopy.

keyTerms.meaning: they are nullified (absorbed into the main item)

steps.whatToRemember: An attachment counts as part of a garment on שבת only if it is unimportant. Significant items like ציצית keep their own identity and count as a load.

phrases.english: Ritual fringes relative to a garment
are significant, and are not nullified.
These (straps) are not significant, and are nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: צִיצִית לְגַבֵּי טַלִּית חֲשִׁיבִי וְלָא בָּטְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 and defends step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the two cases by how significant the attachment is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every attachment would be treated the same, either always a load or never.
steps.terutzMaskana: Significant attachments (ציצית) count as a load. Insignificant ones (canopy straps) become part of the garment.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא allows a trick with the strainer on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that on יום טוב a person may hang up a strainer with the stated purpose of holding pomegranates. Once it is hung, he may then use it to strain wine sediment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: A person may use a trick with a strainer on יום טוב. He hangs it up in order to put pomegranates in it, and then he uses it to strain the wine dregs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that allows a trick (הערמה) to get around the ban on setting up a strainer on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, setting up a strainer for wine on יום טוב is forbidden, but using one that is already hanging is fine. Hanging something for pomegranates is allowed. So he hangs it for an allowed reason, and once it is up, he may strain wine in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Uses a trick or clever excuse (from הַעֲרָמָה) to get around a prohibition
A cloth strainer used to filter wine
Wine sediment, the dregs strained out of the wine

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
A person may use a trick with the strainer
on Yom Tov, hanging it up to put pomegranates in it,
phrases.notes: Hanging it up for pomegranates is a permitted use.

phrases.english: and then he hangs (strains) wine sediment in it.
phrases.notes: Once it is already hanging, straining wine through it is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא: מַעֲרִים אָדָם עַל הַמְשַׁמֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about הערמה, connected to the strainer laws from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may hang a strainer for pomegranates and then use it to strain wine.

steps.title: רב אשי: only if he really hung pomegranates in it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי limits the trick. It only works if the person actually put pomegranates in the strainer first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is only allowed if he actually hung pomegranates in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a condition to the ruling of רבה בר רב הונא. Saying 'it's for pomegranates' is not enough; he must actually use it for pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A trick is only allowed if it is real and visible. Actually putting pomegranates in the strainer shows everyone that it was hung for a permitted use. This condition sets up the question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And that is only when...', a phrase that adds a condition to an earlier ruling

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
And this is only if he actually hung pomegranates in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: וְהוּא דְּתָלָה בָּהּ רִמּוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the ruling in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strainer trick works only if pomegranates were actually hung in it.

steps.title: Why does brewing beer on חול המועד need no proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי with a ברייתא. On חול המועד one may brew beer for the festival, and even someone who already has old beer may use the excuse that he wants new beer, with no visible proof required.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what was taught in a ברייתא? One may brew beer on חול המועד for use during the festival. If it is not for the festival, it is forbidden. This applies to date beer and to barley beer alike. Even if he already has old beer, he may use a trick and drink from the new.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב אשי requires a real, visible act for the strainer trick, when a ברייתא allows a beer trick on חול המועד with only a verbal excuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the beer case, the person already has old beer, so he does not truly need new beer for the festival. Even so, the ברייתא lets him brew by saying he prefers the new beer, and he does nothing to prove it. This seems to contradict רב אשי's demand that the trick be shown by an actual act.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the difference?', used to point out an apparent contradiction between two rulings
Here, חול המועד, the middle days of the festival
Beer, made from dates or barley

phrases.english: What is different from that which was taught:
One may brew beer during Chol HaMoed
for the needs of the festival;
not for the needs of the festival, it is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שֵׁכַר תְּמָרִים וְאֶחָד שֵׁכַר שְׂעוֹרִים.
phrases.english: both date beer and barley beer.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן יָשָׁן —
phrases.english: Even though they have old beer,
he may use a trick and drink from the new!
phrases.notes: No visible act is required to back up the excuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's condition from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's requirement that the trick be backed by a real, visible act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows a beer trick on חול המועד with only a verbal claim, so why does the strainer need actual pomegranates?

steps.title: Beer is not obvious; the strainer is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the beer case, onlookers cannot tell that anything wrong is happening. With the strainer, the forbidden act is plain to see.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the matter is not obvious. Here, the matter is obvious.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by pointing to what onlookers can see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People watching someone brew beer have no idea whether he has old beer at home, so the brewing looks completely permitted. People watching someone strain wine through a strainer he just hung see what looks like a forbidden act. That is why the strainer case needs actual pomegranates to make the permitted purpose visible.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter is evident (it is plain to see what is going on)
There / here, used to contrast two cases

steps.whatToRemember: A trick (הערמה) is tolerated when onlookers cannot see anything wrong. When the act clearly looks forbidden, the permitted purpose must be shown by a real action.

phrases.english: There (beer), the matter is not evident;
phrases.notes: No one knows that he has old beer at home.

phrases.english: here (strainer), the matter is evident.
phrases.notes: Straining wine through a freshly hung strainer looks forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא, הָכָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) based on visibility to onlookers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every trick should follow one rule, so the beer and strainer cases should be the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: A visible act is required only when the trick looks obviously forbidden, as with the strainer, and not when nothing looks wrong, as with the beer.

steps.title: The Rabbis report a scholar's suspicious tricks to רב אשי
steps.stepSummary: The Rabbis tell רב אשי about a תלמיד חכם, רב הונא בן רבי חיון (some say בר רבי חלוון). He plugged a barrel's spout with garlic on שבת, claiming he only meant to store it. He also slept on a ferry that crossed the river so he could check his fruit, claiming he only meant to sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said to רב אשי: Master, look at this young scholar. His name is רב הונא בן רבי חיון, and some say his name is רב הונא בר רבי חלוון. He took a clove of garlic and put it in the spout of a barrel, and said, 'I mean to store it.' He also went and slept on a ferry, crossed to the other side, and inspected his fruit, and said, 'I only meant to sleep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story continuing the theme of tricks. The Rabbis complain to רב אשי about a scholar whose excuses on שבת seem suspicious, which sets up רב אשי's response.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plugging a spout and crossing a river by boat are forbidden on שבת. In each case, the scholar gave a permitted-sounding reason (storing garlic, sleeping) while getting the forbidden result. The Rabbis are asking whether such tricks are acceptable, especially for a תלמיד חכם whom others watch.

keyTerms.meaning: The spout (tap hole) of a barrel
To store it (put it away for safekeeping)
Inspected the fruit (of his field or vineyard)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the Rabbis are just sharing a neat trick. They are reporting behavior that seems questionable and asking רב אשי to judge it. The next step gives his answer.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Ashi:
Let the Master see this young Torah scholar,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בֶּן רַבִּי חִיּוֹן שְׁמֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and Rav Huna ben Rabbi Chiyon is his name,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרַבִּי חִלְווֹן שְׁמֵיהּ,
phrases.english: and some say his name is Rav Huna son of Rabbi Chilvon,
who took a clove of garlic
and placed it in the spout of a barrel,
phrases.notes: This effectively plugs the spout on שבת.

phrases.english: and said: I intend to store it.
And he went and slept on a ferry,
and crossed to the other side and inspected his fruit,
and said: I intended only to sleep!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב אָשֵׁי: חֲזִי מָר הַאי צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of הערמה with a real-life story brought before רב אשי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Rabbis report a scholar's tricks on שבת (plugging a spout and crossing on a ferry) for רב אשי to judge.

steps.title: רב אשי explains why the scholar's trick was different
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the scholar's case involved הערמה in a rabbinic matter. A צורבא מרבנן will not end up doing the forbidden act outright, so no visible proof is needed for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: You are bringing a case of a clever workaround? That workaround was about a rabbinic rule, and a Torah scholar will not come to do the forbidden thing outright.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי responds to the Rabbis' complaint in Step 11. He defends the scholar and explains why his tricks are not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Rabbis thought the scholar's pretexts were improper. רב אשי answers that the prohibitions involved were only דרבנן, and that a צורבא מרבנן is trusted not to drop the excuse and openly do the forbidden act. So we have no reason to stop him from using such a pretext.

keyTerms.meaning: A clever workaround or pretext used to get around a rule
A rule made by the Rabbis, not directly from the Torah
Outright, from the start, without any excuse

steps.whatToRemember: A pretext with no visible proof is tolerated for a תלמיד חכם in a rabbinic matter. For the ordinary person, the strainer trick needs real pomegranates, as רב אשי said.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a key boundary for הערמה. How much proof we demand depends on how serious the prohibition is and on who is doing the act.

phrases.english: He said to them: Are you speaking of a workaround?
It is a workaround in a rabbinic matter,
and a Torah scholar
will not come to do it outright.
phrases.notes: So we do not fear the excuse will turn into open violation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the Rabbis' complaint in step 11 by defending the scholar's conduct.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: rabbinic prohibition plus a Torah scholar, versus an ordinary person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Rabbis assumed the scholar's pretexts were forbidden and should be stopped.
steps.terutzMaskana: A צורבא מרבנן in a rabbinic matter is trusted not to slide into open violation. Others need visible proof.

steps.title: משנה: water over sediment and filtering wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits pouring water over wine sediment so the liquid comes out clear. It also permits filtering wine through cloths or an Egyptian basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: You may pour water onto sediment so that it becomes clear. You may filter wine through cloths and through an Egyptian basket.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists ways of straining wine and sediment that are allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally separating wanted from unwanted material can be the מלאכה of בורר. Here the wine is drinkable even without filtering, so the filtering only improves it and is not real separating. That is why it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian basket woven from palm leaves

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean all straining is fine on שבת. It is allowed because the liquid can be drunk as it is. זעירי will make this limit explicit soon.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One may pour water over the sediment
so that it will become clear.
And one may filter wine through cloths
and through an Egyptian basket.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ נוֹתְנִין מַיִם עַל גַּבֵּי הַשְּׁמָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It continues the theme of straining on שבת and יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouring water over sediment and filtering wine through cloths or a basket are permitted on שבת.

steps.title: משנה: egg in a mustard strainer and making אנומלין
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits putting an egg into a mustard strainer. It also permits making אנומלין, a spiced wine drink, on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may put an egg into a mustard strainer, and you may make אנומלין on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of permitted preparations. It adds the egg in the mustard strainer and the making of a wine-honey-pepper drink.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The yolk passes through the strainer. The ראשונים explain this either as separating yolk from white or as giving the mustard color. Either way, it is not treated as forbidden בורר. Mixing אנומלין is simple food preparation, so the תנא קמא permits it without setting a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A drink of wine mixed with honey and pepper

phrases.english: And one may place an egg in a mustard strainer,
and one may make anumlin on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of permitted actions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An egg may be placed in a mustard strainer, and אנומלין may be made on שבת.

steps.title: משנה: how much אנומלין may be made
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה limits the amount of אנומלין by the day: a cup on שבת, a jug on יום טוב, a barrel on חול המועד. רבי צדוק says it depends on the number of guests.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: on שבת, a cup; on יום טוב, a jug; on חול המועד, a barrel. רבי צדוק says: it all depends on the guests.
steps.whatsHappening: Two תנאים add a disagreement about how much אנומלין a person may prepare.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה ties the amount to how holy the day is. The holier the day, the smaller the amount, to limit extra effort. רבי צדוק sets no fixed measure and says you may make what your guests actually need.

keyTerms.meaning: חול המועד, the intermediate days of the festival

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: On Shabbat, in a cup;
on a Festival, in a jug;
and on the intermediate days, in a barrel.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר הַכֹּל לְפִי הָאוֹרְחִין.
phrases.english: Rabbi Tzadok says: It all depends on the guests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dispute about the quantity of אנומלין permitted in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: the amount scales with how holy the day is. רבי צדוק: the amount follows the number of guests.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows straining liquids that are already drinkable. The two תנאים disagree only about how much אנומלין to make.

steps.title: זעירי: only clear liquids may go into a strainer
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that clear wine and clear water may be put into a strainer on שבת. Murky liquids may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: זעירי said: A person may pour clear wine and clear water into a strainer on שבת without worry. But murky liquids may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. זעירי sets a limit on which liquids may be strained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Clear liquid is already drinkable, so straining it only refines it and is not בורר. Murky liquid is not really drinkable until strained, so straining it is true separating and is forbidden. This explains why the משנה's straining is allowed.

phrases.english: Gemara:
Ze'iri said:

phrases.aramaic: נוֹתֵן אָדָם יַיִן צָלוּל וּמַיִם צְלוּלִין
phrases.english: A person may place clear wine and clear water
into a strainer on Shabbat
and he need not be concerned,
but murky ones, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי: נוֹתֵן אָדָם יַיִן צָלוּל וּמַיִם צְלוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה and limits its straining permission to clear liquids.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clear wine and water may be poured into a strainer on שבת. Murky liquids may not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for straining on שבת. If the liquid is drinkable as it is, straining is allowed. If it is not, straining is בורר.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to allow straining even murky wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges זעירי with a ברייתא. In it, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows stirring up wine with its sediment and pouring the mixture into a strainer on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that a person may stir a barrel of wine, its wine together with its sediment, and put it into a strainer on שבת without worrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict זעירי's rule from the last step. זעירי said murky wine may not go into a strainer, but this source seems to allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי allowed only clear wine in a strainer, because straining murky wine is real separating. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל describes the murkiest possible case: wine deliberately stirred up with its sediment. He still allows it to be strained, which is a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
A person may stir a barrel of wine,
its wine and its sediment,
phrases.notes: Meaning the wine is fully mixed and murky.

phrases.english: and put it into the strainer on Shabbat
and he need not be concerned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks זעירי's ruling from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's rule that murky wine may not be put into a strainer on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly allows straining wine that was deliberately mixed with its sediment, which is the murkiest case possible.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about fresh wine from the presses
steps.stepSummary: זעירי explains that the ברייתא is talking about wine 'between the presses,' meaning new wine fresh from pressing.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי explained it: they taught this about wine at the time of the winepresses.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי defends his rule by narrowing the ברייתא to one special case, new wine at pressing time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fresh wine is commonly drunk with its sediment anyway (רש"י), so straining it is not a real act of separating good from bad. Ordinary aged wine does not fall under this exception, so זעירי's rule still stands for it.
steps.confusionAlert: זעירי is not saying straining murky wine is generally allowed. He limits רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's permission to fresh wine only.

phrases.english: Ze'iri explained it:
They taught this about wine between the presses.
phrases.notes: New, unfermented wine that people drink with its sediment anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows straining any murky wine, which contradicts זעירי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא deals only with fresh wine from the presses, which is drunk with its sediment anyway. זעירי's rule remains for regular wine.

steps.title: Filtering through cloths is allowed only without making a hollow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to filter wine through cloths. רב שימי בר חייא adds that one may not form a hollow in the cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may filter wine through cloths. רב שימי בר חייא said: as long as he does not make a hollow in the cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line of the משנה (from step 13) and adds a condition to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing the cloth into a dip turns it into a container, which is how people filter on a weekday. Keeping the cloth flat makes the act unusual, so it stays permitted on שבת.

phrases.english: One may filter wine through cloths.
Rav Shimi bar Hiyya said:
Provided that he does not make a hollow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה after the זעירי discussion
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Filtering wine through a cloth on שבת is allowed only if no receptacle-like hollow is formed.

steps.title: The Egyptian basket must stay low
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allowed filtering through an Egyptian basket. רב adds that the basket may not be lifted a טפח above the bottom of the vessel underneath.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה also said: and through an Egyptian basket. רב חייא בר אשי said in the name of רב: as long as he does not lift it a טפח off the bottom of the vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and gives רב's condition for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holding the basket high above the lower vessel is the normal weekday way of filtering. Keeping it within a טפח of the bottom makes the act unusual (רבינו יונה), so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian basket made of woven palm leaves

phrases.english: And through an Egyptian basket.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Hiyya bar Ashi said that Rav said:
Provided that he does not lift it
a handbreadth from the bottom of the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues clarifying the משנה, phrase by phrase
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Filtering through an Egyptian basket is allowed only if the basket stays within a טפח of the lower vessel's bottom.

steps.title: A cover may sit over half a barrel, not over all of it
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a perforated cover may be placed over half of a barrel on שבת, but not over the entire barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: this cover, over half the barrel, is permitted; over the whole barrel, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב adds one more practical ruling about filtering, this time about a cover with holes placed over a barrel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the cover spreads over the whole barrel, it looks like a filter set up for straining (רבינו חננאל). Over only half the barrel it does not look that way, so it is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: Straining on שבת is allowed only when it does not look like ordinary weekday filtering. That means only clear wine in a strainer (except fresh wine from the presses), no hollow in the cloth, the basket kept low, and a cover over only half the barrel.

phrases.english: Rav said:
This perforated cover,
over half of the barrel, is permitted;
over the entire barrel, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another filtering-device ruling in the same pattern as steps 19 and 20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A perforated cover over half a barrel is permitted, but over the whole barrel it is forbidden, because it would look like a filter.

steps.title: No straw bundle at a barrel's spigot
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that one may not attach a bundle of straw to the mouth of a barrel's spigot on שבת, because it looks like a strainer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: A person may not attach a straw bundle to the mouth of a barrel's spigot, because it looks like a strainer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds another rule to the list of straining limits on שבת. You may not set up straw at a barrel's spout, because it looks like a strainer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רב's rule about not covering a whole barrel, this rule is about appearance. Straw at the spout acts like a filter, and it looks like a real משמרת, the strainer that may not be set up on שבת. So it is forbidden even though it is not a standard strainer.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle of straw or twigs
A spigot or spout of a barrel
It looks like; it appears as

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A person may not attach a bundle of straw
to the mouth of the spigot (of a barrel),
phrases.notes: The word in parentheses is a textual variant or clarification.

phrases.english: because it looks like a strainer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another limit on straining, after רב's rule in step 21 about covering a barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attaching straw to a barrel's spigot on שבת is forbidden because it looks like a strainer.

steps.title: רב פפא's household poured beer carefully
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב פפא's household would carefully pour beer from one vessel to another so the sediment stayed behind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The members of רב פפא's household would carefully pour beer from one vessel to another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רב פפא's household handled beer on שבת. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gently pouring the clear liquid off the top, without a strainer, leaves the sediment behind. This seems to be allowed because no tool is used to separate. The practice shows that careful pouring was considered acceptable.

phrases.english: The members of Rav Pappa's household
would carefully pour beer from one vessel to another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רב פפא's ruling to a practice in his own household, which sets up a challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carefully pouring beer from one vessel to another so the sediment stays behind was practiced in רב פפא's household.

steps.title: But what about the last drops?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי asks רבינא how this is allowed, since the last drops are poured off from the sediment, which looks like separating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: But there are the last drops!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges the practice of רב פפא's household. When you pour to the end, the last drops come off the sediment, and that looks like separating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring the bulk of the beer is fine. But at the very end, the final drops sit right on top of the sediment. Pouring them off is a careful act of pulling good liquid away from waste, which could count as בורר (selecting).

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא from Difti, an אמורא
The last drops that drip out at the end

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha from Difti said to Ravina:
But there are the final drops!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of רב פפא's household of pouring beer from vessel to vessel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring off the final drops from the sediment is an act of separating good from waste, so it should be forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: The last drops did not matter to them
steps.stepSummary: The answer: in רב פפא's household the last drops were unimportant, so they left them with the sediment and did not separate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The last drops were not significant to רב פפא's household.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב פפא's household did not care about the last drops. They stopped pouring early and left those drops behind with the sediment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The concern only applies if you actually separate the final drops from the sediment. Because the household had plenty of beer, they never tried to save those drops, so no separating took place.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not significant; not considered important

steps.whatToRemember: Careful pouring is allowed as long as you do not try to separate the last drops from the sediment. רב פפא's household simply left those drops behind.

phrases.english: The final drops, to Rav Pappa's household,
were not significant.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִיצוֹצוֹת לְבֵי רַב פָּפָּא לָא חֲשִׁיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation: they never poured off the final drops, so there was no separating.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The household poured to the very end and separated the last drops from the sediment.
steps.terutzMaskana: They left the last drops with the sediment because those drops did not matter to them.

steps.title: The egg in a mustard strainer and יעקב קרחה's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's permission to place an egg in a mustard strainer and introduces a teaching of יעקב קרחה about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the משנה said: One may place an egg in a mustard strainer. יעקב קרחה taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה, which allows putting an egg into a mustard strainer on שבת. It then introduces יעקב קרחה, whose explanation comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting an egg in a strainer lets the yolk pass through while the white stays behind, which looks like separating. Because that seems surprising, the גמרא brings יעקב קרחה to explain why it is permitted. This line only sets up his explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: יעקב קרחה, a sage who taught a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The teaching of יעקב קרחה is not on this amud. The colon means his words come right after, in the next section.

phrases.english: And one may place an egg in a strainer.
Ya'akov Korcha taught:
phrases.notes: His teaching continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ruling of the משנה, after the discussion of straining wine and beer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה permits placing an egg in a mustard strainer on שבת, and יעקב קרחה's explanation follows.
